questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: What is the ideal electrical resistance of an ideal ammeter and an ideal voltmeter, respectively?
questions.explanation: An ideal ammeter is connected in series and must not resist the flow of current; thus, its ideal resistance is perfectly zero. An ideal voltmeter is connected in parallel and must not draw any current away from the circuit component it measures; thus, its ideal resistance is absolute infinity.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.topic: Magnetic field on the axis of a circular current loop
questions.question: A circular current-carrying loop of radius R produces a magnetic field B at its geometric center. If the current flowing through the loop is doubled and its radius is halved, what will be the new magnetic field at its center?
questions.explanation: The magnetic field at the center of a circular loop is B = (μ₀ I) / (2R). If current is doubled (I' = 2I) and radius is halved (R' = R/2), the new field is B' = (μ₀ (2I)) / (2(R/2)) = (2 μ₀ I) / R = 4 * ((μ₀ I) / (2R)) = 4B.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: A straight current-carrying wire is placed in a uniform magnetic field. Under what condition will the magnetic force experienced by the wire be absolutely maximum?
options: When the wire is perfectly parallel to the magnetic field.
When the wire makes an angle of 45° with the magnetic field.
When the wire is strictly perpendicular to the magnetic field.
When the wire makes an angle of 180° with the magnetic field.
questions.explanation: The magnetic force on a current-carrying wire is given by F = I L B sin(θ), where θ is the angle between the wire (direction of current) and the magnetic field. The force is maximum when sin(θ) = 1, which occurs strictly at θ = 90° (perpendicular).

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: An electron and a proton, having the exact same kinetic energy, enter a uniform magnetic field perpendicularly. Which of the following statements is mathematically true regarding the radii of their respective circular paths?
options: The electron traces a circle of larger radius.
The proton traces a circle of larger radius.
Both trace circles of the exact same radius.
The trajectories are straight lines, so radius is undefined.
questions.explanation: Radius r = mv / qB. Since kinetic energy K = mv²/2, momentum p = mv = √(2mK). Thus, r = √(2mK) / qB. Both have the same q and K. Therefore, r ∝ √m. Since a proton's mass is ~1836 times greater than an electron's, the proton has a significantly larger radius.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: What is the correct dimensional formula for the magnetic field B?
questions.explanation: From Lorentz force F = qvB, we get B = F / (qv). Dimensions: Force F = [M L T⁻²]. Charge q = Current × Time = [A T]. Velocity v = [L T⁻¹]. Therefore, B =[M L T⁻²] / ([A T] * [L T⁻¹]) = [M L T⁻²] /[A L] = [M T⁻² A⁻¹].

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: Ampere’s Circuital Law states that the line integral of the magnetic field ∮ B · dl around any closed loop is equal to μ₀ I_enc. If a chosen closed path encloses no net current (I_enc = 0), what can be definitively concluded?
options: The magnetic field B must be zero everywhere along the path.
The line integral ∮ B · dl is zero, but B may not necessarily be zero everywhere.
The magnetic field B must be uniform everywhere along the path.
The path must be a perfect circle.
questions.explanation: Ampere's Law only guarantees that the net integral over the closed loop is zero if I_enc = 0. External currents outside the chosen Amperian loop can produce a non-zero magnetic field along the path, but their net contribution to the closed line integral will always perfectly cancel out to zero.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.topic: Magnetic field on the axis of a circular current loop
questions.question: A straight uniform wire of length L carries a steady current I. When it is bent into a single circular loop, the magnetic field at its center is B₁. When the exact same wire is bent into a circular coil of 3 identical turns and carries the same current I, the magnetic field at its center is B₂. What is the ratio B₂ / B₁?
questions.explanation: For 1 turn, L = 2πR₁ ⇒ R₁ = L/(2π). B₁ = μ₀I / 2R₁. For N=3 turns, L = 3 × 2πR₂ ⇒ R₂ = L/(6π) = R₁/3. The field is B₂ = (μ₀ N I) / 2R₂ = (μ₀ * 3 * I) / 2(R₁/3) = 9 * (μ₀I / 2R₁) = 9 B₁. Thus, B₂ / B₁ = 9.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: A long, thick hollow cylindrical conductor has an inner radius a and an outer radius b. It carries a steady current I uniformly distributed strictly across its solid cross-section (between a and b). Which of the following best describes the graph of the magnetic field magnitude B versus the radial distance r from the central axis?
options: B is zero for r < a, rises non-linearly to a maximum at r = b, and then decays as 1/r for r > b.
B rises linearly from r = 0 to r = b, then decays as 1/r² outside.
B is constant for r < a, then decays exponentially.
B is zero everywhere inside the hollow cavity and the solid material, and only exists for r > b.
questions.explanation: Inside the cavity (r < a), I_enc = 0, so B = 0. Inside the solid material (a < r < b), I_enc ∝ (r² - a²). By Ampere's law, B(2πr) ∝ (r² - a²), so B ∝ (r - a²/r), causing a non-linear rise to a peak at r = b. Outside (r > b), the full current is enclosed, and B = μ₀I / (2πr), which is a 1/r decay.
questions.imagePrompt: A schematic 2D Cartesian graph setup asking for the relationship between Magnetic Field (B) on the y-axis and radial distance (r) on the x-axis. Vertical dashed lines mark r=a and r=b representing the boundaries of a hollow thick cylinder.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: In a cyclotron, a proton is accelerated using an oscillator frequency f. If one wishes to accelerate an alpha particle using the exact same magnetic field, what must the new oscillator frequency be tuned to?
questions.explanation: The cyclotron frequency is f = qB / (2πm). Thus, f ∝ q/m. For a proton: f_p ∝ e/m_p = f. For an alpha particle, charge q = 2e and mass m ≈ 4m_p. Therefore, f_α ∝ 2e / 4m_p = (1/2) * (e/m_p) = f/2.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: A moving coil galvanometer has a coil resistance of 50 Ω and shows full-scale deflection for a current of 2 mA. To convert this galvanometer into an ammeter with a maximum range of 5 A, what is the approximate value of the required shunt resistance?
questions.explanation: Shunt S = (I_g * R_g) / (I - I_g). Given I_g = 0.002 A, R_g = 50 Ω, and target I = 5 A. S = (0.002 * 50) / (5 - 0.002) = 0.1 / 4.998. Since 4.998 is very close to 5, S ≈ 0.1 / 5 = 0.02 Ω.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.topic: Magnetic field due to a current element, Biot-Savart law
questions.question: A wire is bent to form a closed planar loop consisting of two concentric semi-circles of inner radius a and outer radius b, joined by two straight radial segments. A steady current I flows continuously through this loop. What is the exact magnitude of the magnetic field generated at the common center of the semi-circles?
questions.explanation: The straight radial segments have dl parallel to r, so they contribute zero field. The inner semi-circle of radius a produces B_a = μ₀I / 4a (directed inwards). The outer semi-circle of radius b carries current in the opposite rotational direction, producing B_b = μ₀I / 4b (directed outwards). The net field magnitude is the difference: B_net = B_a - B_b = (μ₀ I / 4) * (1/a - 1/b).
questions.imagePrompt: A 2D geometric drawing of a closed wire loop forming a 'C' shape made of two concentric semi-circles. The smaller inner semi-circle has radius 'a'. The larger outer semi-circle has radius 'b'. The ends of the semi-circles are connected by two horizontal straight wire segments lying on the same radial line. Arrows indicate a continuous loop of current 'I'.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.topic: torque on current loop, magnetic dipole
questions.question: An external agent performs a total mechanical work W to slowly rotate a magnetic dipole from its position of stable equilibrium (θ = 0°) to its position of completely unstable equilibrium (θ = 180°) in a uniform magnetic field B. What is the magnitude of the torque required to hold the dipole perfectly at an angle of 90° relative to the magnetic field?
questions.explanation: Work done W = U(180°) - U(0°) = (-MB cos 180°) - (-MB cos 0°) = MB - (-MB) = 2MB. Thus, MB = W/2. The torque at 90° is τ = MB sin(90°) = MB. Substituting MB gives τ = W/2.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: A charged particle of mass m and positive charge q moves with a uniform velocity v = v₀ î through a region containing crossed electric and magnetic fields. The magnetic field is given by B = B₀ ĵ. If the particle passes through this region completely undeflected, what must be the electric field vector E?
questions.explanation: For an undeflected particle, net Lorentz force is zero: F_net = qE + q(v × B) = 0 ⇒ E = -(v × B). The cross product v × B = (v₀ î) × (B₀ ĵ) = v₀ B₀ (î × ĵ) = v₀ B₀ k̂. Therefore, E = -(v₀ B₀ k̂) = -v₀ B₀ k̂.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: Two infinitely long, straight, parallel wires are separated by a distance d. They carry steady currents I and 3I in strictly opposite directions. At what perpendicular distance from the wire carrying current I is the net magnetic field completely zero?
options: d/2 (outside the wires, on the side of current I)
d/4 (outside the wires, on the side of current 3I)
3d/2 (outside the wires, on the side of current I)
questions.explanation: Because the currents are anti-parallel, the fields cancel only OUTSIDE the region between the wires. The null point must be closer to the weaker current (I). Let distance from wire I be x. The distance from wire 3I is (d + x). Equating field magnitudes: μ₀I / (2πx) = μ₀(3I) / (2π(d+x)). Solving: 1/x = 3/(d+x) ⇒ d + x = 3x ⇒ 2x = d ⇒ x = d/2. Thus, it's d/2 outside the wires on the side of current I.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: A moving coil galvanometer has a resistance of 100 Ω and gives full-scale deflection for a current of 10 mA. How can it be successfully converted into a voltmeter with a maximum range of 100 V?
options: Connect a 9900 Ω resistor in series.
Connect a 10000 Ω resistor in series.
Connect a 9.9 Ω resistor in parallel.
Connect a 10 Ω resistor in parallel.
questions.explanation: To convert to a voltmeter, connect a large resistance R in series. Formula: V = I_g(R_g + R). Substituting: 100 = 0.01(100 + R). 10000 = 100 + R. Therefore, R = 10000 - 100 = 9900 Ω in series.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.topic: Magnetic field due to a current element, Biot-Savart law
questions.question: According to the classic Bohr model, an electron revolves in a circular orbit of radius r with a uniform linear speed v. What is the magnitude of the magnetic field B produced strictly at the center of the orbit by this revolving electron?
questions.explanation: The revolving electron forms a current loop. Current I = q/T = e / (2πr/v) = ev / (2πr). The magnetic field at the center of a loop is B = μ₀I / 2r. Substituting I gives B = μ₀(ev / 2πr) / 2r = (μ₀ e v) / (4π r²).

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: A long, solid cylindrical conductor of radius R carries a direct current whose current density J is non-uniform and varies radially as J(r) = J₀(r/R). What is the magnitude of the magnetic field inside the cylinder at a radial distance r (where r < R)?
questions.explanation: Using Ampere's Law: ∮ B · dl = μ₀ I_enc. I_enc = ∫ J(r') 2πr' dr' from 0 to r. I_enc = ∫ J₀(r'/R) 2πr' dr' = (2πJ₀/R) ∫ r'² dr' = (2πJ₀/R) [r³/3]. Substitute into Ampere's Law: B(2πr) = μ₀ (2πJ₀r³ / 3R). Solving for B gives B = (μ₀ J₀ r²) / 3R.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.topic: Magnetic field due to a current element, Biot-Savart law
questions.question: A stiff wire is bent into a perfect regular hexagon of side length a. A steady direct current I flows continuously through the hexagonal loop. What is the exact magnitude of the magnetic field generated precisely at the geometric center of this hexagon?
questions.explanation: The distance d from the center to a segment is the apothem: d = a cos(30°) = a√3 / 2. The angles to the ends of the segment from the perpendicular are θ₁ = 30° and θ₂ = 30°. Field from one segment is B₁ = (μ₀I / 4πd) (sin 30° + sin 30°) = (μ₀I / (4π a√3 / 2)) * (1) = μ₀I / (2π a √3). Total field for 6 segments is B = 6 * B₁ = 6μ₀I / (2π a √3) = 3μ₀I / (π a √3) = (√3 μ₀ I) / (π a).
questions.imagePrompt: A diagram of a regular hexagon made of wire. The side length of the hexagon is explicitly labeled 'a'. Arrows on the wire indicate a steady current 'I' flowing in a continuous loop around the hexagon. A dot clearly marks the exact geometric center.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: A charged particle of mass m and positive charge q is projected directly from the origin (0,0,0) with an initial velocity vector v = v₀ î. A uniform magnetic field B = B₀ k̂ permeates all of space. What are the exact (x, y, z) coordinates of the particle at time t = (π m) / (q B₀)?
questions.explanation: Initial Force F = q(v₀ î × B₀ k̂) = -q v₀ B₀ ĵ. The particle curves down into the -y direction. It executes a circular orbit of radius R = mv₀ / qB₀ in the xy-plane. The center of this orbit must be at (0, -R, 0). The time period for a full revolution is T = 2πm / qB₀. The given time t = πm / qB₀ is exactly T/2 (half a period). After a half period, the particle is diametrically opposite its start. Starting at (0,0,0) with center (0, -R, 0), the diametrically opposite point is (0, -2R, 0) = (0, -2mv₀ / qB₀, 0).

questions.subject: Physics
questions.topic: torque on current loop, magnetic dipole
questions.question: A uniform circular wire loop of radius R and mass m lies flat in the xy-plane and carries a steady current I. A uniform magnetic field B = B₀ î is suddenly switched on. What is the magnitude of the initial angular acceleration α of the wire loop about its diameter? (Assume the moment of inertia of a wire ring about its diameter is 1/2 m R²).
questions.explanation: Magnetic dipole moment M = I(πR²) k̂. Torque τ = M × B = (IπR² k̂) × (B₀ î) = IπR²B₀ ĵ. Magnitude of torque is τ = IπR²B₀. This torque causes rotation about the y-axis (a diameter). Angular acceleration α = τ / I_rot = (IπR²B₀) / (1/2 m R²) = 2πIB₀ / m.
